summary: This informational document defines terminology for benchmarking the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) performance of devices, focusing on basic session setup and registration. Its companion, RFC 7502, gives the methodology.

eli5.summary: If you want to compare how fast different phone-call servers are, you first need to agree on words. This document supplies those words.

questions: what is a device under test in sip
what is registration rate in sip
subtitle: The shared vocabulary for measuring how many SIP calls and registrations a device can handle.

tldr.problem: Vendors report SIP device performance with their own metrics and unstated test conditions, so a service provider cannot fairly compare one SIP server or session border controller with another.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines terms for protocol components, test components, test setup parameters and three black-box benchmarks, all measured on the SIP signaling plane, to be used with the methodology in RFC 7502.
tldr.outcome: Tests become repeatable and comparable, but the benchmarks are meant for a lab and not for production networks.

facts.label: Recommended Establishment Threshold Time
facts.value: Timer B or Timer F (RFC 3261, Table 4)

today: RFC 7501 is an Informational document and the data does not list any RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The test procedures that use these terms are in the companion RFC 7502.

sections.title: Why Benchmark SIP Devices
sections.content:
Service providers and IT organizations deliver VoIP and multimedia services based on the Session Initiation Protocol (RFC 3261). Devices such as SIP servers, Session Border Controllers (SBCs) and Back-to-back User Agents (B2BUAs) report performance with vendor-specific metrics whose test conditions are often unspecified, so they cannot be compared.

This document and its companion RFC 7502 provide black-box benchmarks for devices that include SIP User Agent Client and Server functions and operate in the network's core. Performance here means the capacity of the Device Under Test (DUT) to process SIP messages. Media streams are used only to study how they affect signaling.
sections.eli5: Every shop says its checkout is "fast," but each measures differently. This document says exactly how to measure so the numbers can be compared.

sections.title: What Is and Is Not Covered
sections.content:
The benchmarks cover SIP signaling for network equipment that is RFC 3261 capable: a Registrar, Redirect Server or Stateful Proxy, which may also act as a B2BUA or SBC. The Tester acts as multiple Emulated Agents. Both INVITE and non-INVITE (registration) scenarios are included. Stress conditions, debugging, presence and subscribe-notify extensions, re-INVITEs, session disconnect and IMS-specific scenarios are out of scope.

Media performance is not benchmarked, but whether media is present MUST be noted as a condition of the test. The transport (UDP, TCP, SCTP or TLS) and whether REGISTER and INVITE requests are challenged for authentication must also be recorded. The benchmarks are intended for a laboratory and not for a production network, because some send enough traffic to cause a denial of service.
sections.eli5: The tests only watch how fast the switchboard connects calls. They do not judge how good the voices sound, and they belong in a lab, not on a real network.

sections.title: Protocol and Test Components
sections.content:
Each term is defined in the RFC 1242 template: definition, discussion, measurement units, issues and see-also. The Signaling Plane is where SIP messages are exchanged (SDP is included), and the Media Plane carries the media streams and their control protocols once signaling has set them up.

A Session Attempt is a SIP INVITE or REGISTER request sent by the Emulated Agent that has not received a final response, and an Established Session is one for which the agent received a 200 OK. A Session Attempt Failure is an attempt that does not become established, shown by a 3xx, 4xx, 5xx or 6xx response, or by no response within the Establishment Threshold Time. Overload is the state where a SIP server lacks resources to process all incoming messages. The Emulated Agent is the Tester playing session endpoints, and the Signaling Server is the DUT. The SIP Transport Protocol MUST be reported with any result.
sections.eli5: An attempt is ringing the doorbell, and an established session is someone opening the door. Failure means no one opened up in time.

sections.title: Test Setup Parameters
sections.content:
Five parameters configure the Emulated Agent. Session Attempt Rate is the number of sessions per second it tries to establish through the DUT. Establishment Threshold Time, in seconds, is how long the agent waits before declaring a failure, and it is RECOMMENDED to set it to Timer B or Timer F from RFC 3261, Table 4. Session Duration is how long the dialog should exist, controlled by when the BYE is sent.

Two parameters apply when media is used: Media Packet Size, the fixed number of frames or samples per RTP packet, and Codec Type, the name of the codec. The tests with media are designed for audio codecs, and the document defines no parameters for video codecs. Larger media packets are assumed to need more processor time, which can lower the SIP result.
sections.eli5: These are the knobs on the test machine: how fast to dial, how long to wait for an answer, and how long each call lasts.

sections.title: The Three Benchmarks
sections.content:
Session Establishment Rate is the maximum Session Attempt Rate the DUT can handle for an extended, predefined period with zero failures, in sessions per second (sps). The rate is raised and lowered by the algorithm in RFC 7502 until a load of N attempts completes without failure, where N is recorded in the Test Setup Report.

Registration Rate is the same idea for REGISTER requests, in registrations per second (rps). It is defined separately because it matters to most SIP installations. The RFC's example is an avalanche restart, where hundreds of thousands of endpoints register at once after a power outage. It can also show a difference between registering new endpoints and refreshing existing ones. Registration Attempt Rate is the setup parameter for how many registrations per second the agent sends.
sections.eli5: The score is the fastest speed at which the switchboard can connect calls or sign people in without dropping a single one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Documents of this type do not directly affect the security of the Internet or corporate networks as long as benchmarking is not performed on devices or systems connected to production networks. For security threats to SIP and its media, the RFC points to RFC 3261, RFC 3550 and RFC 3711. It adds that packets with unintended or unauthorized DSCP or IP precedence values may present security issues, but determining the consequences is out of scope.
sections.eli5: Run these tests in a closed practice room, not on the live phone system, because they push very hard.
